title: 1. Present simple forms of 'to be': am/is/are
description: Essential for introducing yourself and others in a digital world.
explanationMarkdown:
The verb to be is the most important verb in English. We use it for names, jobs, and nationalities.

Affirmative
I am (I'm)
You/We/They are ('re)
He/She/It is ('s)
Negative
I am not
You/We/They aren't
He/She/It isn't

Example: 'I'm a digital nomad, but she isn't. She's a designer.'

exercises.explanation: "that man" corresponds to "he", so we use "is".
"your parents" is plural ("they"), so we use "are".
"your name" corresponds to "it", so we use "is".
With the pronoun "you", we always use "are".
With the pronoun "I", we always use "am".
With "she", we use "is".
With "we", we use "are".
In questions with "they", we use "Are" at the beginning.
With "it", we use "is".
With "you" in questions, we start with "Are".

exercises.text: My brother and I ____ good friends.
exercises.explanation: "My brother and I" equals "we" (plural), so we use "are". Do not use "am" just because you see "I".
"The dogs" is plural ("they"), so we use "are".
In questions where the subject is "he", we start with "Is".
"Mary" corresponds to "she", so we use "is".
With "I", we always use "am".
In questions with "you", we start with "Are".

exercises.text: My children ___ playing in the yard.
exercises.explanation: "children" is plural ("they"), so we use "are".
With "she" in questions, we use "Is".
With "I", we always use "am".
"The weather" corresponds to "it", so we use "is".

exercises.text: I ____ not very good at math.
exercises.explanation: With "I", we always use "am".
"This exercise" corresponds to "it", so we use "is".

exercises.text: ____ your friend coming to the party?
exercises.explanation: "your friend" corresponds to "he" or "she", so we use "Is".

exercises.text: We ____ very happy with the results.
exercises.explanation: With "we", we use "are".
"My computer" corresponds to "it", so we use "is".

title: 2. This, that, these, those
description: Talking about objects near you or far away.
explanationMarkdown:
Use these to point to things. This/These are for things 'Here'. That/Those are for things 'There'.

SingularPlural
NearThisThese
FarThatThose

exercises.text: Pointing to a phone in your hand: '________ is my new phone.'
exercises.explanation: If you are holding it, it is 'Near' and 'Singular'.

exercises.text: Pointing to some people across the street: 'Who are ________ people?'
exercises.explanation: People are plural and they are 'Far' away.

title: 3. Possessive adjectives and subject pronouns (I/my, you/your, etc.)
description: My, Your, His, Her... showing ownership.
explanationMarkdown:
These words always come before a noun.

  • I -> My profile
  • You -> Your password
  • He -> His laptop
  • She -> Her website

exercises.explanation: We use 'my' before the noun 'screen'.
'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive form for things.

title: 6. Present simple: I do, I don't, Do I?
description: Talking about things you do regularly.
explanationMarkdown:
Use Present Simple for daily routines. Remember the 'S' for He/She/It!

I/You/We/They: post, follow, like

He/She/It: posts, follows, likes

exercises.text: Complete the sentence: 'He ________ a lot of videos on TikTok.'
exercises.explanation: For 'He', we must add an 's' to the verb in Present Simple.
We use 'don't' (do not) for I/You/We/They.

title: 7. Questions: Word order and question words
description: How to ask for information, WiFi passwords, and directions.
explanationMarkdown:
We use 'Wh-' words at the start of a sentence to get specific information.

  • Who: People
  • Where: Places
  • When: Time
  • Why: Reasons
  • What: Things
  • How: Process/State

Example: 'Where is the meeting?' or 'Who is the new manager?'

exercises.text: ________ do you start work every day?
exercises.explanation: We use 'When' to ask about time or schedule.
'How much' is used to ask about price or quantity.

title: 8. Adverbs of frequency with present simple
description: Always, usually, often... talking about how often you do things.

exercises.explanation: The adverb goes AFTER the verb "to be".
The adverb goes BEFORE main verbs like "go".
The adverb goes BEFORE main verbs like "forget".

In negative sentences, the adverb goes after "don't" or "doesn't".
In questions, the adverb goes between the subject ("you") and the main verb ("work").
"eat" is a main verb, so the adverb goes right before it. No need for "am".
The adverb goes AFTER the verb "to be".
"rains" is a main verb, so the adverb goes right before it.
Longer expressions of frequency like "twice a week" go at the end of the sentence.

title: 9. Object pronouns vs subject pronouns: Me or I, she or her?
description: Me, You, Him, Her, Us, Them... focusing the action.
explanationMarkdown:
These words receive the action. They usually come after the verb.

'If you have the file, please send it to me.'

I -> meHe -> himWe -> us
You -> youShe -> herThey -> them

exercises.text: I like that influencer. I follow ________ on Twitter.
exercises.explanation: 'Him' is the object pronoun for a man.

exercises.text: Our team is great! Join ________ for lunch.
exercises.explanation: 'Us' is the object pronoun for 'we'.

title: 11. At, in, on: Prepositions of time
description: Never miss a deadline or a flight again.
explanationMarkdown:
Time prepositions can be tricky! Here is the remixed cheat sheet:

PrepositionUsage
AtSpecific times (At 5:00, At night)
OnDays & Dates (On Monday, On June 1st)
InMonths, Years, Centuries (In 2025, In July)

exercises.explanation: We use 'on' for days of the week.
We use 'at' for specific clock times.

title: 13. Can, can't: Ability, possibility, permission
description: Discussing your skills and technical capabilities.
explanationMarkdown:
Use can for things you are able to do. It never changes (no 's' for he/she/it!).

Subject + Can + Verb (Base form)

'I can code in Python, but I can\'t speak Japanese.'

exercises.explanation: We use 'Can' to ask about ability or to make requests.
The negative of 'can' is 'cannot' or 'can't'. Never use 'doesn't' with can.

title: 14. Present continuous: I'm doing, I'm not doing, Are you doing?
description: Talking about what is happening right this second.
explanationMarkdown:
Use this for actions happening now. You need the verb 'to be' + 'ing'.

Structure: [Am/Is/Are] + [Verb + ing]

Example: 'I am recording a podcast right now.'

exercises.explanation: If it's happening right now, we need 'is' + verb-ing.

exercises.text: ________ they working from the office today?
exercises.explanation: We use 'Are' for 'They' in the continuous form.

title: 18. Past simple: Regular/irregular verbs
explanationMarkdown:
For regular verbs, just add -ed. It is the same for all subjects!

  • Post -> Posted
  • Like -> Liked
  • Check -> Checked

'I finished the report yesterday.'

exercises.text: I ________ the file to the cloud an hour ago.
exercises.explanation: Regular past simple verbs end in -ed.

exercises.text: Did you ________ the email I sent?
exercises.explanation: In questions with 'Did', the main verb stays in the base form (no -ed).

exercises.text: I ________ a new keyboard online yesterday.
exercises.explanation: 'Buy' is irregular. The past form is 'bought'.

exercises.text: We ________ to a tech conference last month.
exercises.explanation: The past of 'go' is 'went'.

title: 23. A, some, any: Countable and uncountable nouns
description: Talking about quantities when we don't have an exact number.
explanationMarkdown:
Use Some for positive sentences. Use Any for negatives and questions.

  • I have some ideas. (+)
  • I don't have any battery. (-)
  • Do you have any stickers? (?)

exercises.text: I need to buy ________ new headphones.
exercises.explanation: We use 'some' for positive plural sentences.

exercises.text: I didn't receive ________ notification about the meeting.
exercises.explanation: We use 'any' for negative sentences.

title: 24. There is, there are / there was, there were
description: Describing your workspace and local area.
explanationMarkdown:
Use 'There is' for singular items and 'There are' for plural items.

Singular (a/an)
There is a laptop.
There isn't a printer.
Plural
There are two screens.
There aren't any windows.

Modern Example: 'In my office, there is a standing desk and there are many cables.'

exercises.text: ________ any free desks in the coworking space?
exercises.explanation: We use 'Are there' for plural questions (desks).

exercises.text: ________ a coffee shop on the first floor.
exercises.explanation: We use 'There is' for one single thing (a coffee shop).

title: 28. Comparative adjectives: Older than, more important than, etc.
explanationMarkdown:
Use -er for short words and more for long words. Always use than to connect them.

  • Fast -> Faster
  • Cheap -> Cheaper
  • Expensive -> More expensive

'My new laptop is faster than my old one.'

exercises.text: The Pro version is ________ than the Basic version.
exercises.explanation: For long words like 'expensive', we use 'more'.
For short words, we add -er (quicker).
